title: Anchor Date for Cancellations Replaced by HomeFlood — NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)
content:
## Anchor of a replacement cancellation (NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own))

For a cancellation request the named insured signs under Replaced by Private Flood because a Tidemark HomeFlood Private Residential Flood Policies policy recorded as replacing this policy took effect, the anchor rule reads the replacing policy — the customer's active HomeFlood policy whose replaced NFIP policy number is this policy's number — and gives the date the request is dated back to:

| The replacing HomeFlood policy's effective date | Anchor |
|---|---|
| On or after this policy's original effective date and no later than the signing date | The replacing policy's effective date |
| Before this policy's original effective date | This policy's original effective date, because no cancellation reaches back before the policy began |
| No replacing policy in effect (none on record, or its effective date is after the signing date) | The signing date |

*Hypothetical cases.* A HomeFlood policy effective 40 days before the signing date on an NFIP policy that began two years earlier: anchor on the HomeFlood effective date. A HomeFlood policy effective before the NFIP policy itself began: anchor on the NFIP policy's original effective date. A HomeFlood policy taking effect next month: no replacing policy is yet in effect, so the anchor is the signing date.
